query: Earlier refractory high-entropy alloys illustrate persistent trade-offs: MoNbTaW and MoNbTaVW retained good yield strength from 600 to 1600 °C, with MoNbTaVW reaching 842 MPa at 1000 °C, but both had poor room-temperature fracture toughness and high density; HfNbTaTiZr showed room-temperature ductility above 50% and a yield strength of 929 MPa but only 295 MPa at 1000 °C; and as-cast HfMoTaTiZr achieved about 1600 MPa at room temperature and 855 MPa at elevated temperature but retained a density of 10.21 g cm−3. Given the constraint that density must be reduced without sacrificing the strong room- and high-temperature mechanical performance of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr, what single intervention should be tested? Provide a mechanistic hypothesis, predicted outcomes relative to the as-cast baseline, explicit temperature and loading boundary conditions, supporting evidence from the preceding RHEA results, and a controlled experiment with quantitative rejection criteria that could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Substitution of heavy elements with lighter ones in the as-cast HfMoTaTiZr alloy will reduce its density without sacrificing its strong room- and high-temperature mechanical performance.
generation.intervention: Substitution of 20% of Mo with Ti and 10% of Ta with Nb
generation.conditions: Room temperature to 1600 °C, yield strength and fracture toughness loading

generation.predicted_outcome: A reduction in density of at least 5% and a retention of yield strength above 1500 MPa at room temperature and 800 MPa at 1000 °C
generation.baseline: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr alloy with a density of 10.21 g cm−3 and yield strength of 1600 MPa at room temperature and 855 MPa at elevated temperature
generation.boundary: Temperature range of room temperature to 1600 °C and loading conditions of yield strength and fracture toughness
generation.uncertainty: The actual reduction in density and retention of mechanical properties may vary depending on the specific substitution ratio and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the substituted alloy shows a reduction in density of less than 5% or a decrease in yield strength below 1500 MPa at room temperature or 800 MPa at 1000 °C, the hypothesis is rejected
